idiom_name: in / typeof narrowing plus user-defined type guards (function isFlushable(w): w is Flushable)
implementation_notes: TypeScript interfaces are structural, so the capability is the type and the query is a runtime check the compiler learns from: `'flush' in w` narrows a union to the members that have the property, typeof and instanceof narrow by primitive or constructor, and a user-defined type predicate packs a custom check into a function whose return type is `w is Flushable`, so every call site is narrowed without a cast. What replaces the classic structure is this narrowing - the interface is erased at runtime, so the guard is the only place the test exists and it must stay in sync with the interface it claims. Nominal checks remain available: instanceof tests the prototype chain and a class can answer structurally through a Symbol.hasInstance brand, but the in-based structural guard is the idiomatic capability test.
pitfalls: A type predicate is an unchecked assertion: the compiler trusts `w is Flushable` even if the body tests nothing, so a drifting guard silently corrupts every narrowed call site.
'in' only tests property presence and keeps optional properties on both branches: a property explicitly set to undefined still passes, and a non-object operand throws.
instanceof is nominal, fails for structurally valid objects and across realms (separate module instances, iframes), and a Symbol.hasInstance brand is only as reliable as its implementation.
Nothing links the guard body to the declared interface, so adding a member to Flushable does not update the guard - review guards whenever the interface changes.
